messages:
Sam: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a soft-enable of FP8 across a small canary slice on H100 and L40S. Start at 5% traffic, plan to ramp to 20% over 2h if telemetry looks clean. Primary watch: p50/p95/p99, token/sec, kv-hit-rate, kernel selection churn.

Anya: ack. I pinned the per-model latency dashboard and a KV eviction widget. Will watch for >0.5% eviction or >1% p99 regressed.

Mira: quick question — what Transformer Engine flags are we using? nvfuser paths or TE's autotune? Prior runs toggled `TE_USE_NVFUSER` and we saw different kernel picks on L40S.

Sam: good call. Canary config: 
```
TE_FLAGS=--use_transformer_engine --te-autotune=on --prefer-fp8-kernels=true 
KERNEL_SELECTOR=hybrid-risked
KV_WARMUP=enabled
FALLBACK_POLICY=force-int8-longctx
```
We leave nvfuser enabled for H100, but prefer the TE FP8 kernels unless kernel rejects due to occupancy.

Cal: FYI I observed a micro-regression on L40S during an earlier soft roll — p99 up ~0.8% and a subtle throughput dip when the selector flipped from int8->fp8 dotprod. Captured a short trace and profiler snippet.

Sam: do you have the trace? Is it the dotprod slowpath or a KV eviction ripple? We suspected microbatch shape + kv cold misses could amplify the kernel switch penalty.

Cal: attaching excerpt below (copied from profiler):
```
[2026-03-18T12:22:01Z] kernel_choice: fp8_dotprod (tile=32x32)
latency_tokens: 1-128 -> 18.3ms (baseline 17.6ms)
kv_eviction_rate: 0.23% -> spike -> 0.76%
microbatch_shape: [1, 8] -> [2,4] switch correlated
```
Looks like when microbatch packing changed we nudged occupancy low and TE picked a different kernel with worse latency for short tokens.

Mira: that matches a local repro I ran: changing batch shape flips the kernel threshold. Repro script: 
```
python perf/repro.py --model open-7b --quant fp8 --device l40s --batch-shapes "1,8;2,4" --profile
```
The profiling heatmap shows dotprod path longer tail.

Sam: thanks. For the canary I'm adding two mitigations: 1) conservative kernel-safety margin for L40S (force int8 for <64 tokens until we validate), 2) KV warmup ramp to fill hot prefix cache before switching kernels. If either alert fires we auto-roll back the canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-group-17 -> 5% at 2026-03-18T12:34:10Z :rocket:

Anya: I added short-lived alerts: p99 >= baseline*1.03 OR kv-eviction > 0.5% -> notify #eng-runtime + auto-rollback tag. Also telemetry: increased sampling for kernel traces for next 30m.

Mira: I also enabled a profiler hook to capture kernel selection decisions and occupancy stats (nvlink occupancy, SM utilization). If we hit the p99 alert we should have a bisection trace.

Cal: repro script ready for QA. Will run continuous load for 45m against canary to try force the selector flip. Command: 
```
python perf/run_ab.py --model redwood/open-7b --quant fp8 --device l40s --shape-cases "1x8,2x4,4x2" --duration 2700 --capture-trace=kernel
```
I'll post logs if anything interesting pops.

Sam: perfect. If we stay clean for 30m, I'll bump to 20%. If we see the same micro-regression, we keep canary at 5% and iterate on selector heuristics (occupancy threshold, microbatch packing hints). :thumbsup:
